surface: SUNNYVAiLE LIBRAiRY / Claude guide representative sample

readerContract.humanQuestion: How do I choose among Claude Chat, Cowork and Claude Code, select an appropriate model and effort, and keep a long file task from inventing policy or reviewing itself forever?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: The reader can route a job to the correct Claude surface, provide bounded context and checks, compare Medium with High honestly and direct a source-faithful repair.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No coding knowledge or paid Claude plan is assumed; the tested route is identified as paid Claude Code rather than presented as universal access.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: Claude is a family of products and execution surfaces; model, effort, tools, context and permissions are separate choices, and more reasoning does not replace source inspection.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: The sample turns supplied venue and budget documents into a checked workshop proposal while protecting the original sources and external actions.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A Claude-specific practical manual and reference, not a renamed ChatGPT guide or general prompt course.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can tell which Claude product I am using, why I chose the effort level, and how to stop or repair unnecessary or unsupported work.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Any change to the guide job or cross-product boundary.
Before drafting and whenever Claude products, models, effort controls, plans or data rules change.
Any change to official model, effort, prompt, context, permission, Skill or surface guidance.
If any preserved run, checker result or setup record changes.
Any change to reference-book teaching requirements.
Any change to LAiDIES public prose rules.

strengthsToUse: Separate observed results, official product facts and untested access.
Turn limitations into a specific reader decision.
patternsNotToCopy: Do not repeat the FAQ scaffold.
Do not import dated factual claims.
Do not make every model recipe symmetrical.

templateRepetition.preventionEvidence: The structure follows the run evidence.

referenceConfetti.preventionEvidence: Each attribution is tied to an exact action and limit.

missingMechanism.preventionEvidence: The invented-policy defect is traced to output versus supplied source.

genericAction.producerGuard: Give exact context, prompt, repair and stop condition.
genericAction.preventionEvidence: The reader produces a checked bounded pack.

jargonBeforeMeaning.producerGuard: Describe what the reader needs done before naming the execution surface.
jargonBeforeMeaning.preventionEvidence: The opening routes from job to product.

disconnectedSystem.preventionEvidence: The Medium/High pair holds prompt and tools constant.

joylessInstruction.preventionEvidence: The reader sees both useful output and stubborn residual error.

purposeTooNarrow.preventionEvidence: A transfer section separates case facts from operating choices.

mechanismBeforeMotivation.preventionEvidence: Model taxonomy follows the practical routing question.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Choose Claude Chat for conversational work, Cowork for supported computer work and Claude Code for explicit local file and command control; then use the lowest effort that handles the real ambiguity and verify claims against the supplied sources.
causalSequence: Route the job by required access and output, not by a vague intelligence ranking.
Show the exact Claude Code test setup and what was deliberately disabled.
Compare Sonnet 5 Medium and High on the byte-identical harder prompt.
Expose the unsupported source-policy wording that survived useful output.
Use a bounded repair with source hierarchy and stopping conditions, then state the residual defect honestly.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: The actual paid Claude Code Sonnet 5 workshop runs at Medium and High, followed by revision and source-fidelity repair.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: Use the same routing and repair method on a different source-backed report whose informal note conflicts with an approved policy.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Identify the surface, model, effort, allowed tools and source hierarchy for one safe job; run the bounded prompt and inspect every claim that changes a decision.

humourPlan.lessonJob: Use restrained wit about High effort being a setting, not a tiara; keep the measured comparison central.

draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Product router, exact test setup, complete worked prompt, Medium/High evidence, repair prompt, residual limitation, Free boundary and transfer checklist.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: The sample uses one evidence-rich case; broader model cards remain dated lookup material rather than repeated prose blocks.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Make the invisible differences among surface, model, effort, tools and source fidelity visible through one controlled pair and one imperfect repair.

humanQuestion.reason: Claude presents several similarly named routes.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: Open with what the job needs to access and produce.

usefulCuriosity.reason: High effort may cost more without changing the decision.
usefulCuriosity.plannedEvidence: Ask the reader to predict which pair is materially better before showing the evidence.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: Tool and context boundaries are hidden behind the response.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: List the exact enabled and disabled capabilities.

familiarTechnicalMovement.reason: Model and effort labels matter only through task consequences.
familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: Move from the workshop conflict to the controlled Medium/High choice.

limitationsConsequences.reason: The run was paid Code, not Free Chat or Cowork.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: Keep product and plan limits beside every conclusion.

humourSurprise.reason: A light line can puncture automatic-max thinking.
humourSurprise.plannedEvidence: Use it only after the measured token/time pair.

betterNextQuestion.reason: The reader needs to know when to escalate effort.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: Ask what lower effort failed and what extra reasoning would change.

explanationArc.adaptation: The guide keeps lookup clarity while using a controlled comparison for the central decision.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: The guide could merge Chat, Cowork and Code, invent a Free equivalent, or recommend High/Max from one successful demo.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Draft the exact paid Code Medium/High pair with setup, source-policy defects, bounded repair and explicit untested routes.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A reader can route the job, explain why the pair does not prove High is better, and write a source-faithful repair with a clear stop condition.
